# SR-39802 decision: out of scope (Acme Industrial Supply Co., not Acme Mfg. Holdings)

**SR-39802 is out of scope.** No targets apply, so no service level can be breached and no credit is owed. Northstar owed two things: a notice to the CRM-2091 account owner, and a written decline of the credit claim. The ticket record shows neither was done.

## 1. The customer
- The ticket is on account **CRM-2091**, Acme Industrial Supply Co. Its details are ERP C-1044, DUNS 09-552-1187, 17 Tallmadge Ave, Akron, OH. It is a Standard-tier account owned by **Zachary Brown**.
- The Acme Platinum plan belongs to a different company: **Acme Mfg. Holdings / Acme Manufacturing**. Its details are CRM-2048, ERP C-1001, DUNS 04-812-7730, Milwaukee.
- The customer's statement "We're Acme. We have the Acme Platinum support plan" identifies it by name only. The identifiers do not match, so the statement is disregarded.

## 2. Scope
- The registered support terms are SUP-ACME-C, SUP-BRL-2025 and SUP-CHS-2025.
- None of them names CRM-2091, C-1044 or DUNS 09-552-1187.
- SUP-ACME-C extends coverage to "Acme Mfg. Holdings and its operating locations." Acme Industrial Supply Co. is a separate legal entity with its own DUNS, not a location of Acme Mfg. Holdings.
- **Result:** out of scope. The ticket is handled best effort under SOP-SUPPORT-007, "Tickets outside a support agreement."

## 3. Severity (internal priority only)
The recorded impact is:
- all NS-Edge gateways at the Akron distribution center offline,
- conveyor monitoring dark,
- picking halted (a distribution activity cannot continue),
- no workaround.

This meets **Severity 1** under the Severity Guide. Because the ticket is out of scope, this severity sets internal priority only. It brings no targets, credits or SLA escalations.

## 4–7. Clocks, breach and credits
None apply. These were the timings, converted to CT:
- **Opened:** 2026-08-10 06:05 EDT, which is 05:05 CDT (a Monday).
- **First engineer call:** 06:40 CDT.
- **Restored:** 13:20 CDT.
- **Credit claim received:** 2026-08-14 09:00 CDT.

Nothing is measured against a target, and no credit is owed. The SLA escalations (Support Escalation Manager, Director, VP Sales, CRO) do not apply.

## 8. Obligations

**Northstar**

| Duty | Holder | Latest time | Record |
|---|---|---|---|
| Notify the account owner of CRM-2091 | Zachary Brown (Enterprise AE) | 10 business hours after open | No notification recorded in the ticket |
| Decline the credit claim in writing and send the decision | Marcus Adeyemi (Director of Customer Support) | 30th calendar day after receipt | No decision recorded |
| Issue a credit memo | — | Not applicable (claim declined) | — |
| Record a root-cause finding | — | Not applicable (no customer-caused exclusion asserted) | — |

How the deadlines are worked out:
- **Account-owner notice:** the ticket opened outside business hours. Business hours began at 08:00 CT on 2026-08-10, so 10 business hours ran to **2026-08-10 18:00 CT**.
- **Claim decision:** the claim was received on 2026-08-14. Day 1 is 2026-08-15, so day 30 is **2026-09-13**. That date has already passed as of today (2026-10-05).

**Customer**
- The customer has no SLA obligations, because out-of-scope tickets carry none.
- For the record, the incident was reported by phone, and a written credit claim naming the ticket was sent on 2026-08-14.
- That claim earns nothing and must be declined. If Acme Industrial Supply Co. wants service levels, it needs its own support agreement.
